stories.headline: Intel beats Q3 but guides Q4 below estimates on memory-driven PC slump; shares sink 20%+

key_facts.fact: Intel reported Q3 2026 revenue of $16.5 billion, up 21% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.52 (results released Oct 29).
key_facts.excerpt: Third-quarter revenue was $16.5 billion, up 21% year-over-year (YoY). Third-quarter earnings per share (EPS) attributable to Intel was $0.60; non-GAAP EPS attributable to Intel was $0.52.

key_facts.fact: Intel forecast Q4 revenue of $15-16 billion and adjusted EPS of 25 cents, versus analyst expectations of $17.1 billion and 43 cents.
key_facts.excerpt: For the current quarter, Intel said it expects adjusted earnings per share of 25 cents on revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion. Analysts were expecting revenue of $17.1 billion and EPS of 43 cents, according to LSEG.

key_facts.fact: Data center and AI revenue jumped 78% to $7.3 billion, while client computing revenue fell 5% to $8.1 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: revenue in Intel's client computing and physical AI group fell 5% from the same quarter a year ago to $8.1 billion, missing estimates, even as data center and AI revenue jumped 78% to $7.3 billion.

key_facts.fact: CFO David Zinsner said the PC slowdown will continue at least through the first half of 2027; Intel expects 2026 PC unit TAM to fall about 12% and 2027 about 10%, blaming surging memory prices.
key_facts.excerpt: We expect the 2026 PC unit TAM to decline approximately 12%, with second-half units down more than 20%... For 2027, we're planning for the PC unit TAM to decline roughly 10%.

key_facts.fact: CEO Lip-Bu Tan said he was 'disappointed' Intel could not meet strong CPU demand, citing Intel 3 yields, a shortage of advanced organic substrates for EMIB packaging, and a deadly explosion at its Israel fab that will hit Q4 10nm server CPU shipments.
key_facts.excerpt: Tan also pointed to 'an industry-wide shortage of advanced organic substrates' for the company's EMIB chip packaging technology... The third headwind cited by Tan is an explosion that happened earlier this month at an Intel fabrication plant in Israel that killed two workers.

key_facts.fact: Intel expects industry server CPU units to grow more than 30% in both 2026 and 2027, driven by agentic AI.
key_facts.excerpt: We now expect industry server CPU units to grow more than 30% in both 2026 and 2027. Growth would be higher in both years if additional industry supply were available.

key_facts.fact: Intel shares plunged more than 20% in extended trading and were heading toward their worst day in two years, a roughly $128 billion market-value wipeout.
key_facts.excerpt: Why Intel's stock is sinking toward its worst day in two years - and a $128 billion wipeout... the negative impact 'came a little sooner and deeper than we thought,' John Pitzer, Intel's corporate vice president of investor relations, told MarketWatch.

stories.headline: Nvidia in talks to guarantee billions in debt for Nscale's 460MW Anthropic data center

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is in talks to give AI cloud provider Nscale billions of dollars in credit guarantees to support debt funding for a West Virginia data center Anthropic plans to use, The Information reported Oct 29.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia is in talks to offer AI cloud provider Nscale billions of dollars in credit guarantees to support debt funding for a data center earmarked for Anthropic, The Information reported on Thursday

key_facts.fact: The guarantee, likely more than $5 billion by industry estimates, would be a residual value guarantee on the first 460MW building of Nscale's Monarch campus, covering power and construction rather than leases or chips, letting Nscale raise investment-grade construction debt.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia is in talks to give Nscale credit guarantees of likely more than $5B (an industry-estimate-based figure) for debt to build the first 460 MW building of its Monarch campus in West Virginia... The guarantee would be a residual value guarantee on the facility itself (power and construction), not on leases or chips

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has contracted to rent the capacity for about $45 billion; Nvidia has already given about $170 billion in credit support and investment to neoclouds and big customers.
key_facts.excerpt: which Anthropic has contracted to rent for $45B, as disclosed in Nscale's IPO prospectus last month... Nvidia has already given about $170B in credit support and investment to neoclouds and big customers.

key_facts.fact: The deal has not been signed and terms could change; Nvidia is already an investor in UK-based Nscale.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia is an investor in the UK-based cloud provider. The deal has not been signed and terms could still change, the report said

key_facts.fact: Nscale filed for a US IPO in September targeting a valuation of about $30 billion; the site runs Nvidia's Vera Rubin chips.
key_facts.excerpt: The capacity sits at Nscale's Monarch campus in West Virginia and uses Nvidia's Vera Rubin chips... Nscale filed for a US IPO in September, targeting a valuation of about $30 billion, with Nvidia among its investors

key_facts.fact: Nscale's S-1 said that, as of Sept 18, it had not obtained binding commitments for any of the financings required to perform on the Anthropic contract, worth up to about $44.6 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: As of 18 September, the same filing says Nscale has 'not obtained binding commitments for any of the financings required to fund performance', and that all of them 'remain in process'.

stories.headline: Sandisk revenue nearly quintuples to $11B with 8-for-1 split; Kioxia warns NAND price gains slowing

key_facts.fact: Sandisk reported fiscal Q1 2027 revenue of $11.0 billion, up 23% sequentially and 378% year-over-year, with GAAP net income of $8.1 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Fiscal first quarter revenue was $11.0 billion, up 23% sequentially, with GAAP net income reported at $8.1 billion... Revenue $11,031 $2,308 up 378%

key_facts.fact: Sandisk announced an eight-for-one stock split, with post-split trading expected to begin Nov 20, 2026, and guided fiscal Q2 revenue to $12.2-12.6 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Announced today an eight-for-one forward stock split, effective November 19, 2026... Expect second quarter 2027 revenue to be in the range of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion

key_facts.fact: Sandisk's data center revenue was $4.8 billion, up 61% sequentially, and non-GAAP gross margin reached 85.1%; about 60% of revenue growth came from volume and 40% from pricing.
key_facts.excerpt: approximately 60% of the increase attributable to volume growth and 40% to higher pricing. Data center revenue was $4.8 billion, up 61% sequentially... non-GAAP gross margin was 85.1%

key_facts.fact: Revenue of $11 billion beat the $10.7 billion analysts expected.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue: $11 billion, versus $10.7 billion expected

key_facts.fact: Kioxia forecast current-quarter operating profit of ¥2 trillion ($12.7 billion), well short of the ¥2.35 trillion estimate, warning that NAND price rises are easing: average selling prices rose mid-20% in July-September versus 70% the prior quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: said it expects an operating profit of ¥2 trillion ($12.7 billion) in the current quarter, falling well short of estimates for ¥2.35 trillion. That's after the average selling price of NAND flash memory rose a mid-20% in the three months to September, compared with 70% in the prior quarter.

key_facts.fact: Kioxia's July-September revenue rose 40.3% quarter-on-quarter to ¥2.48 trillion and operating profit rose 57.1% to about ¥1.995 trillion; it declared a ¥90 interim dividend.
key_facts.excerpt: For July through September, Kioxia's fiscal second quarter, revenue rose 40.3% from the previous quarter to 2.48 trillion yen. Operating profit increased 57.1% sequentially... Kioxia also announced an interim dividend of 90 yen per share.

key_facts.fact: Kioxia shares fell 7.14% in Tokyo on Oct 30 to ¥13,470, about 60% below their June peak.
key_facts.excerpt: 東京股市鎧俠股價周五仍重挫7.14%，收於13,470日元，自6月歷史高點累計跌幅已達約六成。

stories.headline: China's CXMT posts $8.2B Q3 profit as revenue jumps 613% on AI memory prices

key_facts.fact: ChangXin Memory Technologies reported Q3 net profit attributable to shareholders of 54.4 billion yuan ($8.17 billion) on Oct 30.
key_facts.excerpt: ChangXin Memory Technologies reported net profit attributable to shareholders of 54.4 billion yuan ($8.17 billion) for the three months ended September 30.

key_facts.fact: Q3 revenue reached 118.71 billion yuan ($16.7 billion), up 613.2% year-over-year and 19.3% from the previous quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue for July-September reached 118.71 billion yuan ($16.7 billion), up 613.2% from a year earlier and 19.3% from the previous quarter

key_facts.fact: CXMT, China's largest DRAM supplier, has benefited as SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron prioritise higher-value HBM; sources say it plans limited HBM3E production within two months despite 20-30% yields versus about 70% at SK Hynix.
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT plans to begin limited production of HBM3E chips within two months, despite manufacturing yields of only 20% to 30%, compared with around 70% at South Korea's SK Hynix.

key_facts.fact: Profit growth has slowed sharply: Q3 net profit was only about 1-4% above Q2's 52.84 billion yuan, after more than doubling in Q2, as DRAM price gains moderated.
key_facts.excerpt: The slowdown marks a sharp reversal from the first half, when CXMT's net profit more than doubled to RMB 52.84 billion in 2Q26. Eastmoney attributes the cooling momentum to moderating DRAM price gains

key_facts.fact: The stock sits about 32% below its August peak, following a record 58 billion yuan Shanghai IPO.
key_facts.excerpt: The turnaround follows a record 58 billion yuan IPO in Shanghai that briefly made the firm China's most valuable listed company. Investors remain cautious as the stock sits 32% below its August peak

stories.headline: Agility Robotics SPAC to raise ~$465M with Foxconn-led PIPE, Nasdaq debut set for Nov 5

key_facts.fact: Agility Robotics and SPAC Churchill Capital Corp XI said on Oct 30 the gross capital raise tied to their merger is expected to be about $465 million after the redemption deadline expired.
key_facts.excerpt: following the expiration of Churchill XI's redemption deadline, Agility's gross capital raise in connection with the proposed business combination and related financings is expected to be approximately $465 million, before transaction expenses.

key_facts.fact: The raise includes about $164 million from the SPAC trust, a roughly $201 million PIPE at $10 a share led by Foxconn, and $100 million of equity already received.
key_facts.excerpt: (i) approximately $164 million from Churchill XI's trust account; (ii) approximately $201 million from a common stock PIPE committed at $10 per share, led by Foxconn... and (iii) $100 million of equity funding already received

key_facts.fact: The deal is expected to close Nov 4 after a Nov 2 shareholder vote, with shares trading on Nasdaq as 'AGLT' from Nov 5, making Agility what it calls the only US-listed pure-play humanoid company with active commercial deployments.
key_facts.excerpt: Business combination expected to close on November 4, 2026, subject to Churchill XI shareholder approval; the combined company expected to begin trading on Nasdaq under ticker symbol 'AGLT' on November 5, 2026.

key_facts.fact: Agility has disclosed more than $300 million in committed multi-year orders for its Digit 5 humanoid, with early-access deliveries in 1H 2027 and general availability targeted for end-2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Agility is on track to begin deliveries to early-access customers in the first half of 2027, with general availability targeted for the end of 2027. Agility has previously disclosed more than $300 million in committed multi-year orders for Digit 5.

key_facts.fact: Agility's pipeline includes more than 30 prospective customers; GXO is expanding Digit to two more facilities and AGCO signed for a manufacturing pilot starting in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: an expansion of its relationship with GXO to deploy Digit at two additional facilities, a commercial agreement with AGCO for a manufacturing pilot expected to begin in 2027... Agility's active pipeline includes more than 30 prospective customers

stories.headline: India's AM Intelligence seeks up to $3B in debt to pay for Nvidia Vera Rubin chips

key_facts.fact: Indian AI infrastructure firm AM Intelligence is seeking to raise as much as $3 billion to fund a previously announced purchase of Nvidia's next-generation chips, Bloomberg reported Oct 30.
key_facts.excerpt: AM Intelligence, a Hyderabad-based company, is planning to raise up to $3 billion through bond issues and bank loans to purchase Nvidia Corp's next-generation chips, Bloomberg reported on Friday.

key_facts.fact: The package could combine bonds and bank loans; the firm also expects $300 million in advance payments from potential offtakers, and talks are at an early stage.
key_facts.excerpt: The breakdown between the various options is still being finalized and the firm also expects to get $300 million in advance payment from potential offtakers, the people said. Talks are still in the initial stages and terms could change.

key_facts.fact: AM Intelligence was set up by the founders of renewable energy producer Greenko Group.
key_facts.excerpt: The funding package for the company, established by the founders of renewable energy producer Greenko Group Plc, could comprise of bonds and bank loans, among others

key_facts.fact: The company plans to buy 29,000 Nvidia Rubin chips for 100MW of capacity across India and Malaysia, a $6 billion investment, and aims to add 300MW more over 15 months for more than $20 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: It will buy a total of 29,000 Nvidia's Rubin chips for the 100MW capacity, the company said, adding that it plans to add 300 MW of capacity to market in the next 15 months with an investment of more than $20 billion.

key_facts.fact: AM Intelligence claims to be among the largest committed buyers of Rubin GPUs outside North America.
key_facts.excerpt: India's AM Intelligence claims to be among the largest 'committed buyers' of Nvidia's Rubin graphics processing units outside of North America.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang calls Megaspeed dealings 'normal' as China denies spy report and Warren demands answers

key_facts.fact: In a Bloomberg interview on Oct 29, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said the company's dealings with Singapore's Megaspeed were 'normal and not unusual' and that Nvidia had checked Megaspeed did not divert chips to China: 'We've studied all their deployments of our GPUs and counted every one.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'We've studied all their deployments of our GPUs and counted every one,' he said in the interview. 'And I think the US government also has as well.'

key_facts.fact: Huang said the executive, Huang Le (Alice Huang), is no longer with Megaspeed and that he had not been informed by the US government of its suspicions.
key_facts.excerpt: She's no longer with Megaspeed, he said... The CEO said he hadn't been informed by the US government of its suspicions about Huang Le.

key_facts.fact: China's foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun on Oct 30 called the New York Times report 'groundless speculation' and an attempt to smear China.
key_facts.excerpt: At a regular briefing on Friday, Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said: 'The report in question is based on groundless speculation and is nothing more than an attempt to smear China.'

key_facts.fact: Senate Banking Committee ranking member Elizabeth Warren said on Oct 29 that Huang and Nvidia's board 'owe Congress answers' and urged passage of bills restricting advanced chip sales to China.
key_facts.excerpt: CEO Jensen Huang and Nvidia's board of directors 'owe Congress answers' following reports that Huang developed a close relationship with a suspected Chinese spy... Senate Banking Committee ranking member Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., said in a statement Oct. 29.

key_facts.fact: Singapore police told CNA their investigation into Megaspeed is ongoing; Nvidia said smuggling allegations against Megaspeed were 'thoroughly investigated and debunked last year.'
key_facts.excerpt: the Singapore Police Force (SPF) told CNA on Friday that investigations were still ongoing and it was unable to comment further at this point.

key_facts.fact: Megaspeed said it has appointed external legal advisers to run an internal investigation and told the US government it is willing to cooperate.
key_facts.excerpt: Megaspeed said its current leadership took the allegations seriously and had appointed external legal advisers to conduct an internal investigation. The company also said it had informed the US government that it was willing to cooperate.
